title_en: Pingshan County Labor Employment Administration Bureau v. Tax Authority — dispute over tax administrative handling decision
keywords_en: Administration; Tax Administrative Penalty; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Hebei Province; State Organ; Administrative Penalty Law; Tax Collection and Administration Law; Taxpayer Qualification; Legality of Administrative Penalty Procedure; Application of Hearing Procedure; Revocation of Administrative Penalty Decision; Employment Management Agency Fee; Tax Treatment Decision; Fine; Due Process; Administrative Litigation
full_text_en:
Pingshan County Labor Employment Administration v. Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau — dispute over tax administrative penalty decision

Plaintiff: Pingshan County Labor Employment Administration of Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Xueliang, Director.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Wuqing, Deputy Director of Pingshan County Labor Employment Administration.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Liyong, lawyer of Yinghui Law Firm, Pingshan County.

Defendant: Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau of Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Kang Jingzhong, Director.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yingcheng, Deputy Director of Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Ji Yongyuan, lawyer of Chenyang Law Firm, Pingshan County.

The plaintiff, Pingshan County Labor Employment Administration of Hebei Province (formerly Pingshan County Labor Service Company, hereinafter referred to as the Employment Bureau), dissatisfied with the tax administrative penalty decision of the defendant, Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau of Hebei Province (hereinafter referred to as the Tax Bureau), instituted administrative litigation with the People's Court of Pingshan County, Hebei Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations: This Bureau is an employment management institution undertaking governmental administrative functions, and its fees constitute funds outside the administrative budget. Therefore, this Bureau is not a taxpayer. The defendant ordered this Bureau to pay taxes, and after being refused, imposed a fine on this Bureau by an administrative penalty decision. That decision erroneously applied the law and violated procedures, and we request the People's Court to revoke it.

Defendant's Defense: Although the plaintiff is an employment management institution undertaking some governmental administrative functions, it is a self-financing public institution and should pay taxes according to law. The plaintiff failed to pay taxes in time and should be punished. The People's Court should uphold the administrative penalty decision of this Bureau.

Facts Found by the Court: The plaintiff, the Employment Bureau, is an employment management institution undertaking some governmental administrative functions. From January 1994 to October 1996, it collected labor service management fees, labor service fees, county temporary worker management service fees, temporary worker training fees, and labor market income totaling RMB 578,698.40. On November 29, 1996, the defendant Tax Bureau issued a notice to the Employment Bureau demanding tax declaration within a time limit, and on December 2 and 7, it twice issued notices demanding payment of taxes in arrears of RMB 31,394.71, but the Employment Bureau failed to comply within the prescribed time limits. On December 13, the Tax Bureau, pursuant to Article 46 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If a taxpayer or withholding agent engaged in production or business operations fails to pay or under-pays the tax payable or the tax to be withheld or collected within the prescribed time limit, and fails to pay after being ordered by the tax authorities to pay within a time limit, the tax authorities may, in addition to taking compulsory measures in accordance with Article 27 of this Law to recover the tax that such taxpayer or withholding agent has failed to pay or has underpaid, impose a fine of not more than five times the amount of tax that has not been paid or has been underpaid," issued Tax Administrative Penalty Decision No. 1 (Ping Di Shui Fa Zi [1996] No. 1), imposing on the Employment Bureau a fine equal to three times the unpaid business tax, city construction tax, and education surcharge of RMB 31,394.71, totaling RMB 94,184.13, and ordered payment into the treasury by December 18. The Employment Bureau, dissatisfied, instituted administrative litigation.

The People's Court of Pingshan County held that the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, adopted at the Fourth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress, came into effect on October 1, 1996. The defendant Tax Bureau, as a tax administration authority of a people's government at or above the county level, has the authority to impose penalties for tax-related illegal acts discovered within its jurisdiction. However, such penalties must be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Penalty Law. Before making an administrative penalty decision, the administrative organ shall, in accordance with Article 31 of the Administrative Penalty Law, inform the party of the facts, reasons, and legal basis for the decision, and inform the party of the rights to make statements and defenses, to apply for administrative reconsideration, and to institute administrative litigation. In accordance with Article 36 of the Administrative Penalty Law, it shall collect relevant evidence, and in accordance with Article 37, make investigation records. The Tax Bureau failed to do any of these. Article 42 of the Administrative Penalty Law provides that before making a decision to impose a relatively large fine, the party shall be informed of the right to request a hearing. As to what constitutes a "relatively large" amount, the State Administration of Taxation, in its Measures for Implementing the Tax Administrative Penalty Hearing Procedure (Trial), defined a fine of RMB 10,000 or more imposed on a legal person or other organization as a relatively large amount. These Measures came into effect on October 1, 1996, and the Tax Bureau received the document only 30 days after making the decision against the Employment Bureau. Before the issuance of these Measures, although the law did not clearly define the threshold for "relatively large," it also did not specify that a fine of more than RMB 90,000 was not a relatively large amount. The Tax Bureau's argument that, because the Measures were issued late, the decision was not subject to the hearing procedures under Article 42 of the Administrative Penalty Law, is not sustained. Pursuant to Article 41 of the Administrative Penalty Law, an administrative penalty imposed in violation of the procedures stipulated by that Law cannot be established. According to Item 2 of Article 54 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this decision shall be revoked. The Employment Bureau's allegation that it was not a taxpayer and that the taxation was erroneous, and the Tax Bureau's defense that the plaintiff was a taxpayer subject to taxation, are disputes concerning the substantive merits of the administrative enforcement. It has been established that the administrative penalty decision was procedurally illegal and should be revoked according to law. The court need not continue to hear the dispute on the substantive merits of the administrative enforcement. Accordingly, the People's Court of Pingshan County rendered the following judgment on March 12, 1997:

Set aside the Tax Administrative Penalty Decision No. 1 (Ping Di Shui Fa Zi [1996] No. 1) made by Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau of Hebei Province on December 13, 1996.

The litigation costs of this case in the amount of RMB 6,421 shall be borne by the defendant, Pingshan County Local Taxation Bureau of Hebei Province.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, neither party appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.
